come-up: Rising phase after dosing, before the peak · a phase, not a symptom · pairs with comedown
comedown: Declining phase as effects fade, often with fatigue or low mood · a phase · not withdrawal, not After Effects
deliriant: Hallucinogen subclass (diphenhydramine, datura) producing true delirium and lifelike hallucinations · not psychedelic
dissociative: Hallucinogen subclass (ketamine, DXM, PCP) producing detachment from body and surroundings · not psychedelic
dosage: The amount taken and its tiers · article section and register word · not dose form or packaging
empathogenic: Adjective for entactogen-type effects: emotional openness and warmth · render like entactogenic, the preferred form
entactogenic: Adjective for MDMA-type effects: emotional openness and touch-seeking · site's preferred adjective · empathogenic is its older synonym
hallucinogen: Umbrella class covering psychedelics, dissociatives, and deliriants · never a synonym for psychedelic
harm reduction: Practices that make drug use safer without requiring abstinence · field name, keep one rendering everywhere
psychedelic: Hallucinogen subclass (LSD, psilocybin, mescaline) · not dissociative, not deliriant · not a general word for weird
set and setting: Fixed phrase: mindset and physical environment as determinants of an experience · translate as a pair, keep the order
stimulant: Drug class (amphetamine, caffeine, cocaine) that raises arousal and energy · not an energy drink, not a general adjective
tolerance: Reduced response after repeated use · pharmacological sense, not patience or acceptance
trip report: First-person written account of one drug experience · site content type · not a travel report
withdrawal: Symptoms from stopping a drug after dependence · not comedown, not a bank withdrawal
Threshold: Dose tier 1 of 5: lowest dose with any noticeable effect · an amount, not a doorway or limit
Light: Dose tier 2 of 5 · an amount, not brightness or weight
Moderate: Dose tier 3 of 5: the typical dose · an amount, not a temperament
Strong: Dose tier 4 of 5 · an amount taken, not the potency of the substance
Heavy: Dose tier 5 of 5: dose with significant risk · an amount, not weight
Onset: Duration stage 1 of 6: time until first effects are felt · a delay, not the effects themselves
Come Up: Duration stage 2 of 6: effects rising toward the peak · same concept as the register word come-up
Peak: Duration stage 3 of 6: strongest effects · a time span, not a mountain or maximum value
Offset: Duration stage 4 of 6: effects declining · not compensation, not opposite
After Effects: Duration stage 5 of 6: residual effects after the main experience · not comedown
Total: Duration stage 6 of 6: the whole experience end to end · a length of time, not a quantity
Legal (regulated): Legal status: lawful to possess under rules such as age or licensing · pairs with Prescription only and Restricted
Prescription only: Legal status: lawful only with a medical prescription
Restricted: Legal status: lawful with limits on sale, amount, or place · not illegal
Decriminalized: Legal status: possession is not a criminal offence but may still be penalised · not legal
Not scheduled: Legal status: the substance appears in no controlled-drug schedule · absence of a rule, not permission
Controlled precursor: Legal status: a chemical regulated because it can make a controlled drug · not itself a drug
Illegal: Legal status: possession is a criminal offence
Illegal (analog/blanket ban): Legal status: illegal only because a law covers analogues or whole classes · not named individually
Extremely Low: Risk level 1 of 4 for a harm category · a rating, not a dose
Low: Risk level 2 of 4 · a rating, not a dose or a height
High: Risk level 3 of 4 · a rating · not the slang for intoxicated
No Evidence: Carcinogenicity level: studied with no sign of cancer risk · not the same as Unknown
Unknown: Carcinogenicity level: not studied enough to say · not the same as No Evidence
Possible: Carcinogenicity level: weak or limited evidence of cancer risk
Probable: Carcinogenicity level: substantial evidence short of proof · stronger than Possible
Confirmed: Carcinogenicity level: an established human carcinogen
None: Evidence level: no studies bear on the claim · absence of evidence, not a negative finding
Limited: Evidence level: a few or weak studies
Positive: Evidence level: studies support the claim · a direction, not a mood
Negative: Evidence level: studies contradict the claim · a direction, not a mood
Caution: Interaction tier 1 of 3: combine with care and reduced doses · advisory, not a prohibition
Unsafe: Interaction tier 2 of 3: combination carries real risk and is advised against
Dangerous: Interaction tier 3 of 3: combination can be fatal · strongest warning, keep its full force
Oral: Route of administration: swallowed · clinical register, not spoken
Sublingual: Route: held under the tongue · not Buccal (cheek)
Buccal: Route: absorbed through the cheek lining · not Sublingual (under the tongue)
Insufflated: Route: snorted through the nose · clinical register · pairs with Intranasal
Intranasal: Route: into the nose, snorted or sprayed · clinical register
Inhaled: Route: breathed in as gas or vapour · not Smoked (combustion), not Vaporized specifically
Smoked: Route: burned and inhaled · combustion, not vaporisation
Vaporized: Route: heated without burning and inhaled · not Smoked
Injected: Route: delivered by needle, any site · umbrella for IV, IM, and subcutaneous
Intravenous: Route: injected into a vein · abbreviation IV
IV: Abbreviation of Intravenous · use the target language's standard clinical abbreviation
Intramuscular: Route: injected into muscle · abbreviation IM
IM: Abbreviation of Intramuscular · use the target language's standard clinical abbreviation
IV/IM: Route label: intravenous or intramuscular injection · keep both abbreviations and the slash
Rectal: Route: inserted into the rectum · clinical register
Transdermal: Route: absorbed through intact skin, as a patch or gel
Summary: Substance article section 1: the short overview at the top · heading, not a verb
Overview: Article section: general description of the substance · heading
Identification: Article section: chemical identity, names, and structure · not proof of identity
Classification: Article section: psychoactive and chemical class · heading
Dosage & Duration: Article section: dose tiers and timing tables · keep the ampersand's sense as and
Duration: Article section and table heading: how long effects last by stage
Subjective Effects: Article section: effects as experienced, listed by the Subjective Effect Index · not objective or clinical effects
Pharmacology: Article section: mechanism of action and pharmacokinetics · heading
Interactions: Article section: combinations with other drugs and their risk tier · not social interactions
Harm Potential: Article section: toxicity, dependence, and long-term risk · heading
History & Culture: Article section: discovery, use, and cultural context · keep the ampersand's sense as and
Legality: Article section: legal status by country · not legitimacy
Reagent Testing: Article section: colour reactions with reagent test kits · not laboratory assay
Related Substances: Article section: chemically or pharmacologically similar substances
References: Article section: numbered source list · pairs with Citations and Sources
Citations: Section heading: the inline source markers and their list · pairs with References
Sources: Section heading: where the information came from · not source code
Analysis: Section heading: the site's own assessment of a report or topic · not chemical analysis
Contributors: Section heading and index: people who wrote or edited · not donors
Editorial Review: Section heading: notes from the site's editors about a page's state · not peer review
Personal Commentary: Section heading: the author's own remarks inside a trip report · not the site's view
Meta: Section heading: information about the page itself, such as dates and authorship · not Meta the company
Trip Reports: Section heading and index: first-person experience accounts · not travel
Audio Replications: Section heading: sound-based recreations of effects · replication in the site's sense, not audio copying
Style Variations: Section heading in replications: the same effect drawn in different artistic styles
Replication: An artwork that recreates a drug effect as faithfully as possible · site content type · not copy or repeat
Replications: Plural of Replication and the gallery's name · render like Replication
Replicates: Gallery label: which effect an artwork recreates · verb form of Replication, not laboratory replicates
Replicator: An artist who makes replications · agent noun of Replication
Replicators: Plural of Replicator · render like Replicator
Approved replicator: Credit label: an artist the site has accepted into the gallery · not Verified replicator (identity confirmed)
Verified replicator: Credit label: an artist whose identity the site has confirmed · stronger than Approved replicator
Unattributed: Credit label: the artist is unknown · a status, not a judgement
Artist: Gallery label: the person who made the artwork · not a performer
Artists: Plural of Artist and a gallery filter heading · render like Artist
Artist practice: Gallery filter: the kind of maker (traditional psychedelic artist, generative, cultural) · not a rehearsal
Traditional psychedelic artists: Artist practice: painters and illustrators working in the psychedelic art tradition
Traditional cultural art: Content family: art from indigenous or historical traditions that depicts altered states
Visionary psychedelic art: Content family: art depicting visionary or mystical psychedelic experience · not effect illustration
Dark surrealism: Content family: unsettling surreal art matching dysphoric effects
Optical and perceptual art: Content family: op art and perceptual illusions that mimic visual effects
Experiential replications: Content family: works made to recreate an experience directly · the gallery's core, not illustration
Effect illustrations: Content family: diagrams or drawings that explain an effect · not experiential
Explanatory figures: Content family: figures and charts that explain a concept · not artwork
Unclassified content: Content family: not yet sorted into a family · a status label
Content family: Gallery filter heading: the broad type of artwork · not a family of people
Depicted effect: Gallery filter: which effect the artwork shows
Drug: Gallery filter: which substance the artwork depicts · neutral word, not slang or medicine
Drug class: Gallery filter: the psychoactive class the depicted substance belongs to
Drug in title: Gallery filter: works whose title names a substance
Drug class in title: Gallery filter: works whose title names a drug class
Psychedelics: Gallery filter: works depicting psychedelic effects · class name, plural
Dissociatives: Gallery filter: works depicting dissociative effects · class name, plural
Deliriants: Gallery filter: works depicting deliriant effects · class name, plural
Other: Catch-all filter value: everything not in the named groups
Viewing mode: Gallery filter: whether the effect is seen with eyes open or closed
Open-eye: Viewing mode: effects seen with eyes open · pairs with Closed-eye
Closed-eye: Viewing mode: effects seen behind closed eyelids · pairs with Open-eye
Media: Gallery filter heading: the medium of the work (image, video, audio)

Disregard Everything I Say: The site's parent project and channel name · proper noun, never translate

SEI: Abbreviation of Subjective Effect Index · keep in Latin letters
PsychonautWiki: External reference site · proper noun, never translate
TripSit: External harm-reduction site · proper noun, never translate

Liebermann: Reagent test named for a person · use the transliteration reagent kits use

Hofmann: Reagent test named for a person · use the transliteration reagent kits use
